reframing:
REFRAMING C (coverage sieve over N=7 sectors + Bonferroni/Brun truncation). Natural number N=7 (the sectors). Let A_j = {x in [0,1): no e in E sends frac(e*x) into sector j} = "sector j is never hit by the orbit." Then {x: orbit hits ALL 7 sectors} = complement of union_j A_j, so

  p0(E) = 1 - meas(union_{j=0}^6 A_j) = sum_{S subset {0..6}} (-1)^|S| m_S(E),  m_S = meas(intersect_{j in S} A_j) = meas{x: every sector in S is missed}, m_empty=1.

INCLUDED/EXCLUDED: we sieve out the configurations that miss at least one sector. m_S is the measure of x missing every sector in S. Bonferroni cumulative partial sums give ALTERNATING bounds. With U = meas(union A_j) = sum_k (-1)^{k+1} Sigma_k, Sigma_k = sum_{|S|=k} m_S, the truncations give p0 >= 1-Sigma_1, p0 <= 1-Sigma_1+Sigma_2, p0 >= 1-Sigma_1+Sigma_2-Sigma_3, ... So EVEN cumulative levels are UPPER bounds on p0 (the side we want for p0<=cap), ODD are LOWER.

TWO EXACT VANISHING FACTS that shape the sieve: (1) Because 0 in E (the co-offset cluster always contains 0), sector 0 is ALWAYS hit (e=0 fixes frac(0*x)=0 in sector 0), so A_0 is empty and every m_S with 0 in S vanishes; the sieve effectively runs over the SIX sectors {1,...,6}. (2) m_S=0 for |S|=7 (can't miss all 7), and over the 6-sector framing m_{1..6} is the single top term and Sigma_7=0 — so the sieve TERMINATES at level 6.
whatItBuys: It isolates p0 as a finite alternating sieve that PROVABLY terminates at level 6 (Sigma_7=0; only the single top term m_{1,2,3,4,5,6} survives at the deepest level), and it makes manifest that "hit all 7" = "hit all of {1..6}" once 0 in E. It cleanly explains the apex/truncation phenomenon (THM-551) at the sector level: the deepest nonvanishing term m_{1..6} (the all-6-missed measure) is exactly the "everything lands in sector 0" event, of measure 1/49 for these clusters. It does NOT, however, isolate a low-level upper bound below cap (see proofRoute) — that is the decisive negative finding.

The sieve's only even-level upper bound that beats cap is the FULL level 6, which equals p0 exactly (since Sigma_7=0) — so it certifies nothing beyond the exact value. Intermediate truncations overshoot: L2 ~1.18 (Sigma_2 too big), L4 ~0.48-0.62 (still 0.05-0.10 above cap), and Brun's error term (the first omitted Sigma_5) is bigger than the overshoot, so truncating earlier provably cannot reach cap. The CORRECT next lemma the reframing isolates: a uniform height-weighted bound on the SUMMED two-far residual R_2 = sum_{pairs} [I_B(f,f') - Phi_2(B)], NOT a per-packet 1/7 bound. Concretely: (i) per-pair |I_B(f,f')-Phi_2| <= H(f,f') := (height-weighted signed relation bound) with H -> 0 off-resonance like V(B)/min(f,f') and saturating at <=0.014 on the consecutive resonance (verified, THM-548 sec 3b); (ii) sum over C(r,2) pairs, but at most O(r) pairs can be simultaneously resonant (a far set has few small relations -- Freiman/dissociation), so the resonant contribution is O(r * 0.014) and the off-resonant contribution is O(C(r,2) * V/min(f) ), both absorbed by the margin(P_r) which GROWS in r (0.13,0.17,0.28,0.38,0.48 at r=1..5). Then sum_{s>=3} R_s IS genuinely 1/7-suppressed per the apex hierarchy (verified: |R_3|/|R_2| = 0.10..0.68, always <1) so the s>=3 tail is a true geometric remainder. Net route: close r=2 via the simultaneous peel (THM-548 sec 5, done to cutoff W~26), then for r>=3 use (margin grows) + (R_2 bounded by #simultaneous-resonances * 0.014 + dissociated tail) + (R_{>=3} geometric). The one genuinely open piece is the count/size bound on simultaneous two-far resonances among r far runners (the d>=2 relation-lattice / Freiman dimension penalty, HYP-2678/2637).
